messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert -> api-gateway-us-west-2 showing 502/504 spike, error rate ~7% over last 5m. Paging @oncall-lee :rotating_light:

oncall-lee: I'm oncall, joining bridge now. Starting quick triage.

sre-alex: grabbing recent ingress logs and proxy metrics. Will paste top errors in a sec.

runtime-maya: fyi telemetry shows request latency climb first, then 502s. Possible backend connection resets or pool exhaustion.

infra-nick: checking gateway pod CPU/mem and connection pool metrics. If connection pools exhausted, we should open fallback routing.

oncall-lee: team, plan: 1) confirm spike scope (regional vs global) 2) activate fallback-to-eu pool for non-EU customers 3) throttle retries at edge 4) hold deployments.

cs-jordan: CS note: we see elevated errors on dashboards for ~12 customers; top 3 are API-heavy integrations. I'll open a runbook ticket for manual outreach if error >10% next 15m.

sre-alex: logs show many upstream resets (502) to model-backend-x86-1, code snippet:

```
proxy: upstream_reset_by_peer, id=abc123, conn_reset=true
upstream: 10.2.5.12:8080 refused_stream
```

runtime-maya: that backend instance is on a dedicated pool that hit max connections. We have KV cache warm; unlikely cache issue. Suggest scale backend pool + add circuit-breaker.

infra-nick: scaling gateway and backend pools now: kubectl scale deployment gateway-proxy --replicas=12
kubectl scale deployment model-backend-x86 --replicas=8

oncall-lee: enabling short-term routing fallback to eu region for non-GDPR traffic. This will reduce load on us-west.

oncall-lee: also lowering proxy retry attempts to 0 for immediate failfast to reduce duplicate load.

product-sam: rolling back the canary deployed 2 hrs ago? Recent deploys show slight increase in CPU on that backend pool. Recommend hold and investigate.

runtime-maya: Agree. Pausing rollouts and pinning traffic.

cs-jordan: customer impact update: error spike started ~08:12 UTC, peaked 08:18 UTC, now at 3.2% after mitigations. Active customers affected: 9 (errors >1%).

sre-alex: telemetry after scale + fallback: 502s dropping. Current 5xx rate 1.8% in last 2m. Latency still elevated ~250ms p95 (baseline 120ms).

infra-nick: tracing suggests connection pool backlog on model-backend-x86-1; we've increased pool size and recycled a few unhealthy pods.

oncall-lee: action items: (a) continue monitoring for 15m (b) keep deployments paused (c) infra to follow up with healthcheck/auto-restart thresholds (d) CS to prepare outbound notes if >5% persists.

product-sam: postmortem owner? Recommend eng-sre + runtime to co-own follow-up; include canary rollout config and connection pool tuning.

runtime-maya: I'll own model backend tuning and quantize ops that may affect connection patterns.

oncall-lee: marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will keep the channel open for updates. Please post any regressions here. :white_check_mark:

cs-jordan: I'll draft a brief customer-facing status and tag the impacted accounts.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> MITIGATED by oncall-lee at 08:28 UTC.

sre-alex: leaving logs and key metrics in the incident doc (link) and will start a short RCA runbook after stabilization.

oncall-lee: thanks all. Stand down unless the error rate climbs back above 3%.
